John Ternus became Apple's new CEO this week, and the Financial Times today published a profile interview providing the latest information about his life and his reputation among Apple employees and partners.

John Ternus's latest interview reveals more details about Apple's new CEO

John Ternus has taken over as Apple's new CEO in the past few days, with Tim Cook transitioning to the role of Executive Chairman.

9to5Mac editor Chance Miller has compiled a comprehensive introduction about Ternus for everyone, covering his educational background, early career, public statements, and more.

However, a new interview published today by the Financial Times adds more details and insights to this story.

Regarding Ternus's reputation within Apple, the report says he "is known inside the company as highly capable and quietly pragmatic." A partner at one of Apple's major suppliers feels the same way:

A former Apple executive told the Financial Times that Ternus "is relatively unknown within the company outside the hardware division." However, it is unclear when that executive left the company, as Ternus's standing internally has clearly risen over the past year.

Tim Cook has said Apple "genuinely wants to make this transition as good as it can be." And judging by one small anecdote in the interview, that intent seems to have been felt internally.

Beyond these insights, the Financial Times also adds some important details about Ternus's extremely low-key private life. The interview notes that he is married, has children, and was born and raised in California.

To learn more about Apple's new CEO, please refer to our previous related coverage:

  • Who is John Ternus? Everything you need to know about Apple's next CEO
  • John Ternus makes first appearance as CEO, revealing work priorities
  • Read the full internal memo John Ternus sent to Apple employees on his first day in office

We will see Ternus make his first public appearance as CEO next week at Apple's big iPhone event.
